name: hard-browser-tasks
description: 12 bounded, multi-step research and UI tasks with explicit acceptance criteria. Fixed paper/release targets; no login or purchases. Not a WebVoyager benchmark score. See hard-suite.md for reference checks and limitations.

tasks.ques: Use arXiv advanced search to find papers matching the unquoted words graph neural networks in the Abstract field, across all archives, with Submission date (most recent) from 2024-01-01 to 2024-01-03. Include cross-listed papers. Inspect the complete result set and identify every paper with more than five authors.
criteria: Show the Abstract field, both date bounds, most-recent-submission date mode, and all-archives scope in browser evidence; do not substitute Title, original submission, or announcement date.
Report the total search result count and enumerate every result's arXiv ID and author count, including papers excluded by the author threshold.
For every qualifying paper, provide its title, arXiv URL, and complete author list. State the number of qualifying papers.

tasks.ques: Compare arXiv Title and Abstract searches for the unquoted words graph neural networks. Use all archives, include cross-lists, and restrict Submission date (most recent) from 2024-01-01 to 2024-01-03. Run Title first, then refine that search by changing only the field to Abstract. Compare the actual paper sets, not just their sizes.
criteria: Browser evidence must show Title followed by the refined Abstract search, with the same query text, dates, date mode, and archive scope.
Report both result counts and all arXiv IDs in each result set.
List the intersection, Title-only IDs, and Abstract-only IDs. Equal counts must not be treated as proof that the sets are identical.
Include a source URL for each search and for each paper appearing in only one set.

tasks.ques: Find the original arXiv records for Attention Is All You Need, BERT: Pre-training of Deep Bidirectional Transformers for Language Understanding, and Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks. Build a comparison table using the records, not prior knowledge.
criteria: Open all three matching abstract pages and provide each exact title and arXiv ID/URL.
For each paper, report the complete author count, first and last authors, primary subject category, and original v1 submission date.
Report the highest version number submitted before 2024-01-01 and that version's date for each paper; distinguish original submission from revision dates.
Order the table by original submission date, oldest first, and identify which paper has the most authors.

tasks.ques: Audit the complete arXiv submission histories, through 2023-12-31, of Attention Is All You Need and Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks. Read both history sections and reconcile their revision counts.
criteria: For both papers, enumerate every version submitted before 2024-01-01 with version number and UTC calendar date, without omissions or duplicates.
Report total versions and total revisions separately for each paper; the original v1 submission is not a revision.
List the calendar years in which each paper was revised after v1, and identify the paper with more revisions.
Include both abstract-page URLs and browser evidence of the full history sections.

tasks.ques: Compare sentence-transformers/all-MiniLM-L6-v2, sentence-transformers/all-mpnet-base-v2, and intfloat/e5-small-v2 for English retrieval. Select every model among these three that has embedding dimension at most 384, a documented default maximum input length of at least 512 tokens/word pieces, and an MIT or Apache-2.0 license.
criteria: Inspect all three model cards and provide a table of full model ID, license ID, embedding dimension, and documented default truncation length, with a model-card URL per row.
Do not confuse embedding dimension, parameter count, transformer position capacity, and the documented sentence-encoder input limit.
For each model, explain which numerical or license constraint it satisfies or fails, then give the complete qualifying set.
For any selected E5 model, state the documented query and passage prefixes needed for retrieval. Do not run inference.

tasks.ques: Audit sentence-transformers/all-MiniLM-L6-v2 and sentence-transformers/all-mpnet-base-v2. Compare their model cards' truncation limits with sentence_bert_config.json and 1_Pooling/config.json, using the browser file viewer.
criteria: Open both model cards and both named configuration files in each repository; include all six source URLs.
For each repository, report the card's default truncation length and sentence_bert_config.json max_seq_length, and say whether they agree.
Report word_embedding_dimension and every pooling_mode_* boolean present in each 1_Pooling/config.json, grouped by repository.
Explain which pooling mode is enabled and keep dimensions separate from maximum input length. Do not execute code or download model weights.

tasks.ques: Use the stanfordnlp/sst2 dataset viewer to compare its train and validation splits. Inspect train, switch to validation, and then return to train. Do not substitute another SST-2 repository.
criteria: Browser evidence must show train, validation, then train, with the active split visible each time.
Report exact train and validation row counts from the dataset card or viewer, not rounded values such as 67.3k.
For rows with idx 0 and 1 in each split, report the numeric label and corresponding sentiment name. Verify the mapping from the displayed schema/card.
Identify the viewer's data column names, provide split-specific source URLs, and finish with the train split selected.

tasks.ques: In the stanfordnlp/sst2 train dataset viewer, collect every row with idx 95 through 104 inclusive. This crosses the default 100-row preview boundary. Use the viewer's next-page or row-navigation controls to inspect both sides of the boundary.
criteria: Keep the train split selected and record browser evidence for rows on both sides of the page boundary; do not use an API or downloaded dataset.
Return exactly ten unique rows sorted by idx, each containing idx, numeric label, and sentiment name. Do not report row positions from another split.
Give the positive and negative counts for those ten rows and verify that they sum to ten.
Include viewer source URLs for the pages or row ranges used.

tasks.ques: From the pallets/flask 3.1.0 release, trace the partitioned-session-cookie and secret-key-rotation features to their original issues and implementing pull requests. Distinguish a closed issue from a merged pull request.
criteria: Find the 3.1.0 release notes and identify the exact configuration key introduced for each feature.
For each feature, open its linked original issue and implementing PR, and report their numbers, titles, URLs, and respective closed/merged states.
Verify the implementation relationship using the issue timeline or PR discussion; do not assume the issue number in the release notes is the implementation PR.
Include the release URL and keep the two feature-to-issue-to-PR mappings distinct. Do not post, react, or modify anything.

tasks.ques: Compare psf/requests v2.32.2 and v2.32.3 release notes. Trace the custom HTTPAdapter migration in v2.32.2 and both bug fixes in v2.32.3 to their linked pull requests.
criteria: Open both release pages and report their release dates and source URLs.
For v2.32.2, distinguish the renamed private method, its new public replacement, and the separately deprecated older public method; include the migration PR number and URL.
For v2.32.3, enumerate both listed bug fixes and their distinct PR numbers/URLs. Keep the custom SSLContext and missing ssl-module problems separate.
Open all three linked PRs and verify each title and merged state. Do not infer merge status merely because a PR is closed.

tasks.ques: Find the closed 3.1.0 milestone in pallets/flask and audit its complete closed-item inventory. Separate merged pull requests, unmerged closed pull requests, and closed issues.
criteria: Verify the milestone title, closed state, closure date, and displayed open and closed item counts.
Enumerate every closed item's number, URL, and one of: merged PR, unmerged closed PR, or closed issue. Inspect ambiguous items individually and any additional pages if present.
Report totals for all three groups and reconcile their sum with the milestone's closed-item count; no duplicates or omitted items.
Do not assume every closed item is an issue or every closed PR was merged. Include the milestone URL.

tasks.ques: Use GitHub's file viewer to compare pallets/flask pyproject.toml at tags 2.3.3 and 3.1.0. Open the file at 2.3.3, switch the ref to 3.1.0, and report the packaging requirement changes without substituting the main branch.
criteria: Browser evidence must show the same pyproject.toml path at both specified tags, with 2.3.3 inspected before 3.1.0. Finish on the 3.1.0 file.
Report requires-python and the full direct project.dependencies list for each tag, including version constraints and any environment markers.
Identify changed dependency constraints and dependencies added or removed; distinguish direct runtime dependencies from build-system requirements and optional extras.
State whether the declared Python requirement permits Python 3.8 in each tag. Include both tag-specific file URLs. Do not execute code.
